title: fix(scenarios): keep a working-day card's dates on working days on every run date
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9KP2AnyfX9ZJYh48bUsyqbo)_

Fixes #33793

Clause-②: yes (widening) — new optional key `ScenarioCardSchema.workingDays` (`.`)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：场景卡可以声明 `workingDays: true`;运行器平移这种卡的日期时，今天仍落在运行当天，其余日期按整工作日平移，不再按整天。请假卡 `leave_balances` 声明了它，并把 31 条落在周末的审批日期挪到下一个工作日。
- 为什么改：上一个 PR 按整天平移后，7 个运行日里有 6 天会把请假日落到周末(最多 126/307 条),应用只算周一到周五，于是 6 条真值和余额跟卡上的数字对不上，问句里的「周三」也会变成「周日」。
- 风险与回滚：只动 `packages/qa/scenarios`(运行器、加载器、卡格式多一个可选键，属放宽)和这张卡;别的 6 张带日期的卡不声明，行为不变。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/run-date.ts` 的 `moveFor`(两种平移的分叉点),`src/loader.ts` 的 `checkWorkingDays`,卡里 31 行 `decided_on`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios exec vitest run test/runner/run-date.test.ts`,34 项全过;其中连续 7 个运行日(2026-11-15 到 11-21)各一项。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

**Step 1, measured first.** On `origin/main` (895783a1e), over seven consecutive run dates 2026-11-15 (a Sunday) to 11-21, the whole-day rebase puts this card's working days on weekends on six of the seven: only 11-18 (delta 49, whole weeks) is clean. When a working day lands on a weekend, the meaning changes in three places:

- **Request days.** The card's prompt has the app sum a request's day lines "Monday to Friday only". Read that way over the moved seed, 60 to 84 of the 120 requests no longer have the seeded `days`.
- **Balances and truths.** 17 to 22 balances' `used_days` move with them, and 6 of the 10 truths change: `approved_days`, `top_annual_takers`, `approved_days_last_month`, `annual_days_by_department`, `remaining_annual_by_department`, `lowest_annual_remaining`. The persona truths change too. Only the two approval-step questions, the medical-note count and the unanswerable one hold.
- **Asks.** `file_and_submit_from_text` asks for weekend leave on 3 of the 7 dates ("Sunday 13 December" on 11-15). `half_day_on_draft` targets a line that falls on a Saturday or Sunday on 2 of the 7, and its request has a weekend line on a third.

The other dated cards: the open library has 7 dated cards, not 9 (`crm_account_with_contacts` and `project_with_tasks` have no `asOf`). Searching the 6 others for weekday names, `weekday`/`weekend`/`working day`/`business day`, `周X`, `工作日` and `周末` gives **0 hits**. Their seeds already hold 2 to 256 weekend dates each, so none keeps to working days. `leave_balances` is the only one, with 12 hits.

**Step 2, the fix.** Three ways to fix this, with the measured reason for the choice:

- **A whole-week delta** is ruled out by the card. It keeps weekdays only by putting the prompt's today up to three days off the run date.
- **Snapping each moved date to its nearest working day** breaks multi-day leave. On the same seven dates, 36 to 62 requests get two day lines on one date (0 only on 11-18).
- **Moving the card by whole working days** keeps every Monday-to-Friday span intact. This is the one shipped.

Changes:

- **The card format** (`src/schema.ts`): an optional card key, `workingDays: true`, declared by the author, never inferred. It widens what `ScenarioCardSchema` (exported from `.`) accepts, hence `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The new helpers in `run-date.ts` (`shiftWorkingDays`, `workingDaysBetween`, `onWorkingDay`) reach no `exports` subpath: `run-date.ts` is imported only by `src/runner/cli.ts`, and the built `index`, `runner`, `score`, `score-full` and `export` declarations hold none of them (`ScenarioCardSchema` found in `index.d.ts` as the positive control).
- **The loader** (`src/loader.ts`, `checkWorkingDays`) refuses such a card in two cases:
  - it has no `asOf`;
  - `asOf`, or any ISO date under `run` or `iterate`, falls on a Saturday or Sunday. The refusal names the path and the weekday. A weekend `asOf` would be counted as the Friday before it, so that Friday and `asOf` would both move onto the run date.
- **The rebase** (`src/runner/run-date.ts`, `moveFor`). A card without the key moves exactly as before. A card with it moves like this:
  - `asOf` goes onto the run date itself, so the prompt's today is still the run date. The rebase also refuses a weekend `asOf` on such a card (it throws) rather than map two dates onto one.
  - Every other date moves by `workingDaysBetween(asOf, runDate)` whole working days (`shiftWorkingDays`). A weekend run date is read as the Friday before it.
  - So a date before the card's today lands before the run date, and a date after it lands after the run date. Consecutive working days stay consecutive, and N working days between two dates stay N.
  - Ask-text dates move the same way, and their weekday names are written again (`shiftTextDates` now takes either a day count or the card's move).
  - Truths are recomputed over the moved seed, as before. `scopeFigures` still stay, because the move maps distinct dates to distinct dates.
- **`docs/qa/scenarios/leave_balances.json`:**
  - It declares `workingDays: true`.
  - The seed rule said "decided the day after submission" and "two days after", which put 31 approval decisions on a Saturday or Sunday. It now says "the working day after" and "two working days after".
  - Exactly those 31 `decided_on` values move. A recomputation of every step from its request's `submitted_on` changes no other row, and no truth reads `decided_on`.
- **The two READMEs:**
  - `docs/qa/scenarios/README.md`, the card authors' guide, gains a paragraph. The runner moves a card's dates onto the run date, so an author must not rely on a fixed calendar date or a weekday name. A card on working days declares `workingDays`.
  - `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`: its run-date bullet stated the old limit ("keeps to them only when the delta is whole weeks"). It now states the contract.
- `.changeset/33793-working-day-rebase.md`: `@objectstack/scenarios` patch.

## Tests

`packages/qa/scenarios/test/runner/run-date.test.ts`, 34 tests (was 18).

**New: whole working days.** These check `shiftWorkingDays` and `workingDaysBetween`:

- across a weekend, a month end, a leap day and a year boundary, and around the epoch week;
- each against an independent walk over the calendar, one day at a time.

**New: `leave_balances` on seven consecutive run dates (2026-11-15 to 11-21).** For each date:

- `asOf` is the run date.
- Every moved date, apart from a value that is the card's today, is a working day.
- A date before the card's today lands before the run date, and a date after it lands after.
- Each request's Monday-to-Friday day lines, read independently over the moved seed, sum to its `days`. Each balance's `used_days` equals its approved requests' days.
- Every non-calendar truth and every persona truth equals the card's own figure.
- The English and Chinese asks name working days only. Each named weekday is that date's own, and the dates are the ones the operation's values and expected day lines carry.
- The half day the draft's ask names is the date of the line it targets.

**New: loader refusals.** A copy of the card with one leave day on Saturday 2026-07-04 is refused once, at `run.seed.leave_day[0].leave_date`. The same copy without `workingDays` is not refused for it. A copy whose `asOf` is Saturday 2026-10-03 is refused once, at `asOf`. A copy without `asOf` is refused.

**New: a weekend `asOf` counterexample.** A copy with `asOf` Saturday 2026-11-14 and a leave day on Friday 2026-11-13, run on Wednesday 2026-11-18: counted from that Friday, the Friday itself would move onto 11-18 with `asOf`. The rebase throws on it (`asOf 2026-11-14 is a weekend`), and the loader refuses the same card once, at `asOf`.

**Forced edits to existing tests**, named:

- `every dated card, rebased onto each run date › run on DATE` (nine tests). The leaf check and the calendar-window reading-back used one whole-day delta for every card. They now read each card's move independently: whole days, or for a `workingDays` card a walk over working days. Only the title words changed otherwise.
- `the asks that write a date say the moved one…`: the leave pins were the defect. On 2026-11-15 they now read "Friday 11 December and the morning of Monday 14 December" (was Sunday 13) and "(3 December)" (was 5 December).

**Ablations**, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each restored with blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`:

- The loader's `asOf` check deleted: 2 of 34 red, the two loader refusals of a weekend `asOf`.
- The rebase's weekend-`asOf` guard disabled: 1 of 34 red, the rebase counterexample.
- At the first round's head, with `moveFor` forced to the whole-day branch, 16 of the 31 tests went red. Those were the 9 every-dated-card runs, the ask pins, and 6 of the 7 seven-day runs; 11-18 stayed green, as the measurement predicts (blob 500440c7 to 2899d999).

## Deviations

- `packages/qa/scenarios/src/schema.ts` is outside the claim's file surface. The card-level flag the claim allows can only live there, because the card is a strict object the loader parses against that schema (+6 lines, one optional key). The seat accepted this.
- The key's name, `workingDays: true`, was proposed here with `rebase: "working_days"` and `dates: "working_days"` as alternatives. The seat chose `workingDays`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Weekend run dates.** On a Saturday or Sunday run, the card's other dates move as they would for the Friday before it. So 11-20 and 11-21 seed identically, and the moved data ends up to two days nearer the run date than the card wrote it. Nothing seeded before the card's today moves past the run date, which is #33753's invariant.
- **Hire dates still move.** The rebase moves `hire_date` (whole days before, working days now). `leave_year` (`2026/27`) and the 1 July service rule live in the prompt and the strings, which are not moved. On a run date about nine months or more after `asOf`, the moved leave falls into the next leave year while the balances still say 2026/27. This was the same before this change and is a property of the shipped rebase, not of the weekday defect. Noted, not filed.
- The `$comment` seed rule ("working day … of July") still describes the card's own dates. Like the prompt, it is never moved.
